Wednesday, November 4, 2026

Space & Defense Daily — Wednesday, Nov 4, 2026

Russia hits Ukraine's grid with its biggest energy strike of the year as NATO and the US, UK, France and Germany meet in Brussels on security guarantees; a leaked EU work programme says Europe's 2030 defence-readiness goal is at risk; the Space Force stands up a special operations component and seeks up to five cislunar seed satellites.

← NewerThu, Nov 5, 2026All briefingsOlder →Tue, Nov 3, 2026
NATOEuropean UnionUnited StatesEuropean spaceGlobal space & defense

Top stories: Russia launched its biggest strike on Ukraine's energy system this year (289 drones, 17 ballistic and 59 cruise missiles) just as NATO confirmed a Brussels meeting this week with the US, UK, France and Germany on security guarantees for Ukraine. A leaked draft of the European Commission's 2027 work programme warns Europe's 2030 military-readiness goal is "at risk" despite record spending. And the Space Force activated SPACEFOR-SOC under US Special Operations Command while asking industry about up to five cislunar "seed" satellites.

NATO

  • NATO spokesperson Allison Hart confirmed alliance officials will meet representatives of France, Germany, the UK and the US in Brussels later this week on security guarantees and a "just and lasting" end to the war, following talks in Miami and Oslo; US envoy Steve Witkoff says trilateral talks follow next week in the UAE. (Ukrainska Pravda via Yahoo News)
  • After seven strikes on cargo ships near Romania and Bulgaria in October and a Greek container ship sunk by naval drones in Bulgaria's EEZ, the widening Black Sea maritime war is becoming a major test for NATO, which has deployed patrol aircraft, radars and drones to the area. (Reuters via CNA)
  • Nordic allies are wrestling with how to counter Russian sabotage, drone incursions and GPS jamming in the Baltic without stoking escalation, leaning on Baltic Sentry, Task Force X-Baltic and closer Swedish-Finnish surveillance cooperation. (Defense News)
  • Montenegro's and Albania's defense ministers want NATO to send hybrid-response experts to help counter Russian disinformation; diplomats say allies are open to it, though it would need consensus. (Politico Europe)
  • About 2,800 personnel from 12 European nations will run Exercise Koalicja in Poland from Nov. 9 to 22, rehearsing how a UK- and France-led reassurance force would deploy to Ukraine after a peace deal; Turkey will lead the maritime element. (BBC News)

European Union

  • A leaked draft of the Commission's 2027 work programme, due to be adopted today, says the 2030 readiness goal is "at risk" despite €418 billion in 2025 defence spending, and proposes a European Instrument for Strategic Enablers (airlift, refuelling, space and cyber) plus a European Security Emergency Protocol. (Euronews)
  • The second SAFE call puts the remaining €21.3 billion in defence loans on offer to all member states, with requests due Nov. 30 and priority on air and missile defence, drones, counter-drone and ammunition, including joint buys with Ukraine; about €13.5 billion has been disbursed so far. (European Commission)
  • At the EU-UK security and defence dialogue, Kaja Kallas and UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting prepared for the EU-UK summit in two weeks; Kallas said there is no UK SAFE deal and a possible "SAFE two" is not yet on the table. (EEAS)
  • Germany is weighing a role in the UK-Italy-Japan GCAP fighter after the collapse of the FCAS fighter effort, and Airbus is preparing talks with BAE Systems, though Merz cautioned Berlin may not decide by early 2027. (The Defense Post)
  • Airbus has scrapped its Wingman drone to meet Germany's faster timeline, prioritising the U760 Ravenstorm collaborative combat aircraft for 2032 service, while the Kratos-partnered U740 Valkyrie targets a 2029 requirement and a Eurofighter teaming flight next year. (Breaking Defense)
  • At Euronaval in Paris, Fincantieri and Leonardo signed a letter of intent to strengthen their Orizzonte Sistemi Navali joint venture, prime on Italy's DDX destroyers and FREMM EVO frigates. (Leonardo)

United States

  • The Space Force activated Space Forces Special Operations Command (SPACEFOR-SOC) at MacDill AFB on Monday, the first new USSOCOM service component since 2006, fielding small Space Special Warfare Teams with space, cyber and intelligence experts. (Military Times)
  • A Nov. 2 RFI says the Pentagon is "notionally" interested in up to five cislunar seed satellites, ready to fly by late 2029 with initial operations by 2031, to inform a future proliferated cislunar constellation. (Aviation Week)
  • The Army awarded Lockheed Martin a $1.08 billion cost-shared deal ($660.4 million government, $423 million Lockheed) to develop the PAC-3 Edge interceptor for its Future Interceptor program, with testing from 2027 and fielding targeted for 2031. (The Defense Post)
  • With the midterms held Nov. 3, Congress now has about 20 House and 22 Senate session days before the Dec. 11 CR expires; CSIS expects any reconciliation defense money to land nearer the $60 billion in budget resolutions than the $350 billion requested, which also funds most of Golden Dome. (CSIS)
  • Space Systems Command is weighing eight AI projects, from orbital targeting to Vandenberg range scheduling, for up to $12 million in Fight Tonight funding, with winners named Nov. 13. (ExecutiveGov)
  • Former Army Secretary Dan Driscoll, who resigned in August, has joined OpenAI as senior counselor for national security modernization. (DefenseScoop)
  • SpaceX is now targeting Friday, Nov. 6 at 4:46 p.m. PT for the classified USSF-432 Falcon 9 launch from Vandenberg. (SpaceX)

European space

  • ESA opened a new AI Hub at its ECSAT site on the Harwell campus in the UK, backed by the UK Space Agency, to develop AI for satellite connectivity, spectrum use, 6G and direct-to-device, and cybersecurity. (ESA)
  • ESA signed NAVISP contracts with Norway's Testnor, Norse Navigation and Rift Dynamics on jamming- and spoofing-resilient positioning, including a GNSS interference data library and drone navigation for GNSS-denied conditions. (ESA)
  • ESA's Hera planetary-defense probe can now separate Dimorphos from Didymos for the first time, with detailed images of the DART-impacted moonlet due Nov. 25. (Space.com)

Global space & defense

  • Russia hit substations, transmission lines and power plants across 10 oblasts in its biggest attack on Ukraine's energy this year, including a substation critical to the Khmelnytskyi nuclear plant; DTEK lost generation at three thermal plants. (Kyiv Independent)
  • The State Department approved a possible $2.1 billion sale of 500 PAC-3 MSE interceptors to Ukraine, funded by Canada, Germany and Norway, but Zelensky warns deliveries are years away and is asking for stockpile transfers now. (Kyiv Independent)
  • China launched a Lijian-2 Y2 rocket from the Dongfeng commercial pilot zone on Nov. 3, placing a new satellite group in orbit. (Xinhua)
  • Starfish Space's first Otter servicing spacecraft failed shortly after launch when its fault-protection system blocked communications. (SpaceNews)
  • Rocket Lab's Electron launched a radar-imaging satellite for Japan's iQPS as the vehicle nears its 100th mission. (SpaceNews)
